## The survey offer {#survey}

::: {.two}
::: {}
A market-research firm offers a demand survey for **CNY 5 million**. It reports either **favorable (F)** or **unfavorable (U)**.

Its track record gives the chance of a favorable report in each true state. The survey is useful but not perfect: in one low-demand case out of five it still reports F.
:::
::: {}
```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>True demand</th><th class="num">Prior</th><th class="num">P(F | state)</th><th class="num">P(U | state)</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Low</td><td class="num">0.3</td><td class="num">0.2</td><td class="num">0.8</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Medium</td><td class="num">0.5</td><td class="num">0.6</td><td class="num">0.4</td></tr>
    <tr><td>High</td><td class="num">0.2</td><td class="num">0.8</td><td class="num">0.2</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```
:::
:::

::: {.route-question}
To use the report, we need the reverse: P(state | F) and P(state | U). Bayes' theorem gives them.
:::

## Bayes: revise the probabilities {#bayes}

```{=html}
<div class="formula"><p>P(<i>s</i> | F) = P(F | <i>s</i>) · P(<i>s</i>) / P(F), &nbsp;&nbsp; P(F) = Σ<sub><i>s</i></sub> P(F | <i>s</i>) · P(<i>s</i>)</p></div>
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>State</th><th class="num">Prior</th><th class="num">Joint with F</th><th class="num">Posterior given F</th><th class="num">Joint with U</th><th class="num">Posterior given U</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Low</td><td class="num">0.30</td><td class="num">0.06</td><td class="num">0.115</td><td class="num">0.24</td><td class="num hit">0.500</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Medium</td><td class="num">0.50</td><td class="num">0.30</td><td class="num">0.577</td><td class="num">0.20</td><td class="num">0.417</td></tr>
    <tr><td>High</td><td class="num">0.20</td><td class="num">0.16</td><td class="num hit">0.308</td><td class="num">0.04</td><td class="num">0.083</td></tr>
    <tr><td><b>Total</b></td><td class="num">1.00</td><td class="num"><b>P(F) = 0.52</b></td><td class="num">1.000</td><td class="num"><b>P(U) = 0.48</b></td><td class="num">1.000</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

[A favorable report raises P(high) from 0.20 to 0.31. An unfavorable report raises P(low) from 0.30 to 0.50.]{.note-line}

## What the survey is worth {#evsi}

::: {.two}
::: {}
```{=html}
<div class="formula"><p>EVSI = 71.6 − 56 = <b>15.6</b></p></div>
```

EVSI is the expected value with the survey minus the expected value without it. Efficiency = EVSI / EVPI = 15.6 / 39 = **40%**.

The survey is worth up to CNY 15.6 million. At CNY 5 million, buying it adds **10.6 million** of expected value.
:::
::: {}
::: {.route-question}
The survey has value only because an unfavorable report changes the choice from A to C. Information that cannot change a decision is worth nothing to that decision.
:::
:::
:::

[With a risk-averse board (R = 100), the survey still pays: its certainty equivalent is 36.4 against 34.8 without it, and after a favorable report the board picks B, not A.]{.note-line}

## Change the survey {#evsi-explorer data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="ev">
  <div class="w-controls">
    <label class="w-slider">P(F | low) <strong id="ev-l-v">0.20</strong><input type="range" id="ev-l" min="0" max="1" step="0.05" value="0.2"></label>
    <label class="w-slider">P(F | medium) <strong id="ev-m-v">0.60</strong><input type="range" id="ev-m" min="0" max="1" step="0.05" value="0.6"></label>
    <label class="w-slider">P(F | high) <strong id="ev-h-v">0.80</strong><input type="range" id="ev-h" min="0" max="1" step="0.05" value="0.8"></label>
    <label class="w-slider">Survey cost <strong id="ev-c-v">5</strong><input type="range" id="ev-c" min="0" max="30" step="1" value="5"></label>
  </div>
  <table class="wide" id="ev-table"></table>
  <div class="w-readout" id="ev-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('ev');
  if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  const prior = [0.3, 0.5, 0.2];
  const O = [['A', [-120, 80, 260]], ['B', [-40, 60, 150]], ['C', [10, 40, 70]], ['D', [0, 0, 0]]];
  const f = (x) => x.toFixed(1).replace('-', '−');
  const ids = ['l', 'm', 'h', 'c'];
  function draw() {
    const v = Object.fromEntries(ids.map((k) => [k, +document.getElementById('ev-' + k).value]));
    ids.forEach((k) => { document.getElementById('ev-' + k + '-v').textContent = k === 'c' ? v.c : v[k].toFixed(2); });
    const lik = [v.l, v.m, v.h];
    const pF = prior.reduce((s, p, i) => s + p * lik[i], 0), pU = 1 - pF;
    const post = (rep) => prior.map((p, i) => (rep === 'F' ? p * lik[i] / pF : p * (1 - lik[i]) / pU));
    const best = (q) => O.map(([k, pay]) => [k, pay.reduce((s, x, i) => s + x * q[i], 0)]).reduce((m, x) => (x[1] > m[1] ? x : m));
    const rows = [];
    let ev = 0;
    for (const [rep, pr] of [['F', pF], ['U', pU]]) {
      if (pr < 1e-9) { rows.push(`<tr><td>Report ${rep}</td><td class="num">0.00</td><td colspan="3">never happens</td></tr>`); continue; }
      const q = post(rep), b = best(q); ev += pr * b[1];
      rows.push(`<tr><td>Report ${rep}</td><td class="num">${pr.toFixed(2)}</td><td class="num">${q.map((x) => x.toFixed(2)).join(' · ')}</td><td class="num hit">${b[0]}</td><td class="num">${f(b[1])}</td></tr>`);
    }
    document.getElementById('ev-table').innerHTML = '<thead><tr><th>Report</th><th class="num">Probability</th><th class="num">Posterior low · medium · high</th><th class="num">Best option</th><th class="num">EMV</th></tr></thead><tbody>' + rows.join('') + '</tbody>';
    const evsi = ev - 56, net = evsi - v.c;
    document.getElementById('ev-out').innerHTML = `EVSI = ${f(ev)} − 56 = <b>${f(evsi)}</b> (efficiency ${Math.max(0, evsi / 39 * 100).toFixed(0)}%). ` +
      (net > 1e-9 ? `<span class="best">Buy: net gain ${f(net)}</span>` : `<span class="best">Do not buy: the survey costs more than it is worth</span>`);
  }
  ids.forEach((k) => document.getElementById('ev-' + k).addEventListener('input', draw));
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

[Try P(F | state) = 0.5 in every state: the report then says nothing, and EVSI falls to zero.]{.hint}

## Screening with a Pugh matrix {#pugh}

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Criterion</th><th>LFP Li-ion (datum)</th><th>Vanadium flow</th><th>Aqueous organic flow</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>LCOS</td><td>S</td><td>−</td><td>−</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Safety</td><td>S</td><td class="hit">+</td><td class="hit">+</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Footprint</td><td>S</td><td>−</td><td>−</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Cycle life</td><td>S</td><td class="hit">+</td><td>S</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Supply risk</td><td>S</td><td>−</td><td class="hit">+</td></tr>
    <tr><td><b>Count</b></td><td>0</td><td>2 plus, 3 minus</td><td>2 plus, 2 minus</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.bridge}
A Pugh matrix compares each option with a reference, criterion by criterion: better (+), same (S) or worse (−). It screens quickly, but it treats every criterion as equally important.
:::

[Ratings in Sessions 2 and 3 are illustrative, written for the CellCo case, not an assessment of any product.]{.source}

## AHP in four steps {#ahp}

::: {.elements}
::: {.el}
[1 · Hierarchy]{.label}
Goal, then criteria, then alternatives.
:::
::: {.el}
[2 · Pairwise comparisons]{.label}
For each pair of criteria: how much more important is one? Scale 1 (equal) to 9 (extreme).
:::
::: {.el}
[3 · Weights]{.label}
Geometric mean of each row, normalized to sum to 1 (close to the principal eigenvector).
:::
::: {.el .key}
[4 · Consistency]{.label}
CI = (λ~max~ − n)/(n − 1), CR = CI / RI. Accept if CR < 0.10 (RI = 1.12 for n = 5).
:::
:::

::: {.bridge}
Comparing two things at a time is easier than scoring five at once, and the consistency ratio tells you when the judgments contradict each other.
:::

```{=html}
    <tr><td>LFP Li-ion</td><td class="num">9</td><td class="num">5</td><td class="num">9</td><td class="num">6</td><td class="num">6</td><td class="num">0.330</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Vanadium flow</td><td class="num">6</td><td class="num">8</td><td class="num">4</td><td class="num">9</td><td class="num">4</td><td class="num hit">0.342</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Aqueous organic flow</td><td class="num">4</td><td class="num">9</td><td class="num">3</td><td class="num">6</td><td class="num">8</td><td class="num">0.329</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.bridge}
Each rating is divided by its column total, then weighted. Vanadium flow leads, but the three scores lie within 0.013 of each other. A result this close says more about the weights than about the technologies.
:::

## Activity 2 · Stakeholder AHP {#act2 .activity data-hold="true"}

[Groups of 4 · 30 minutes · role cards and the next slide]{.act-label}

::: {.prompt}
Each member takes one role and fills in the ten pairwise comparisons from that role's point of view.
:::

1. Roles: **CFO** (cost), **safety officer**, **plant manager** (space and uptime), **sustainability lead** (supply chain).
2. Combine the four judgments for each pair by geometric mean, for example (3 × 1/2 × 2 × 1)^1/4^.
3. Enter the group's comparisons on the next slide. Is CR below 0.10? Which technology wins?
4. Each group reports its weights and winner. We compare across the room.

::: {.selfstudy}
Studying alone: fill in the comparisons twice, once as the CFO and once as the safety officer, and compare the winners.
:::

## Enter your comparisons {#ahp-explorer data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="ahpw">
  <div class="ahp-grid" id="ahp-pairs"></div>
  <div class="w-readout" id="ahp-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('ahpw');
  if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  const C = ['LCOS', 'Safety', 'Footprint', 'Cycle life', 'Supply risk'];
  const S = [[9, 5, 9, 6, 6], [6, 8, 4, 9, 4], [4, 9, 3, 6, 8]];
  const ALT = ['LFP Li-ion', 'Vanadium flow', 'Aqueous organic flow'];
  // Board defaults, as slider positions: +k means row criterion is (k+1) times as important; -k the reverse.
  const base = { '0-1': -1, '0-2': 4, '0-3': 1, '0-4': 2, '1-2': 6, '1-3': 2, '1-4': 3, '2-3': -2, '2-4': -1, '3-4': 1 };
  const pairs = Object.keys(base);
  const toVal = (k) => (k >= 0 ? k + 1 : 1 / (1 - k));
  const lab = (k) => (k === 0 ? 'equal' : k > 0 ? (k + 1) + '×' : '1/' + (1 - k));
  document.getElementById('ahp-pairs').innerHTML = pairs.map((p) => {
    const [i, j] = p.split('-').map(Number);
    return `<label class="ahp-pair"><span class="ahp-l">${C[i]}</span><input type="range" min="-8" max="8" step="1" value="${base[p]}" data-p="${p}"><span class="ahp-r">${C[j]}</span><b data-v="${p}"></b></label>`;
  }).join('') + '<button type="button" class="ahp-reset" id="ahp-reset">Reset to the board</button>';
  const sums = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4].map((c) => S.reduce((s, r) => s + r[c], 0));
  function draw() {
    const A = C.map(() => C.map(() => 1));
    root.querySelectorAll('input[data-p]').forEach((el) => {
      const [i, j] = el.dataset.p.split('-').map(Number), k = +el.value;
      A[i][j] = toVal(k); A[j][i] = 1 / toVal(k);
      root.querySelector(`b[data-v="${el.dataset.p}"]`).textContent = lab(k);
    });
    const gm = A.map((r) => Math.pow(r.reduce((s, x) => s * x, 1), 1 / 5));
    const tot = gm.reduce((s, x) => s + x, 0), w = gm.map((x) => x / tot);
    const Aw = A.map((r) => r.reduce((s, x, j) => s + x * w[j], 0));
    const lam = Aw.reduce((s, x, i) => s + x / w[i], 0) / 5, CR = ((lam - 5) / 4) / 1.12;
    const score = S.map((r) => r.reduce((s, x, c) => s + (x / sums[c]) * w[c], 0));
    const bi = score.indexOf(Math.max(...score));
    document.getElementById('ahp-out').innerHTML =
      'Weights: ' + C.map((c, i) => `${c} <b>${w[i].toFixed(3)}</b>`).join(', ') +
      `. CR = <b style="color:${CR < 0.1 ? '#0F6E6B' : '#BE654C'}">${CR.toFixed(3)}</b> ${CR < 0.1 ? '(consistent)' : '(revise your judgments)'}<br>` +
      'Scores: ' + ALT.map((a, i) => `${a} ${score[i].toFixed(3)}`).join(', ') + `. Winner: <span class="best">${ALT[bi]}</span>`;
  }
  root.addEventListener('input', draw);
  document.getElementById('ahp-reset').addEventListener('click', () => {
    root.querySelectorAll('input[data-p]').forEach((el) => { el.value = base[el.dataset.p]; }); draw();
  });
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

[Move a slider toward the criterion that matters more. The middle position means equal importance.]{.hint}

## How fragile is the ranking? {#act2-debrief}

::: {.two}
::: {}
Hold the board's other judgments in proportion and change one weight:

- LFP overtakes vanadium flow once the LCOS weight passes **0.32** (board: 0.27).
- Aqueous organic flow overtakes vanadium flow once the safety weight passes **0.56** (board: 0.43), or the LCOS weight falls below **0.16**.
:::
::: {}
```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Typical role weights</th><th>Winner</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>CFO, LCOS 0.50</td><td>LFP Li-ion</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Plant manager, footprint 0.30</td><td>LFP Li-ion</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Safety officer, safety 0.60</td><td>Aqueous organic flow</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Sustainability lead, supply 0.40</td><td>Aqueous organic flow</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```
:::
:::

::: {.bridge}
AHP does not remove disagreement. It shows where the disagreement is, so the board argues about weights instead of conclusions.
:::

## What we learned {#debrief}

::: {.takeaways}
::: {.tk}
A decision tree folds back from right to left: expected value at chance nodes, best branch at decision nodes.
:::
::: {.tk}
Bayes' theorem turns a survey's track record into posterior probabilities. The first survey's EVSI is CNY 15.6 million, 40% of EVPI, so it is worth its CNY 5 million price.
:::
::: {.tk .key}
AHP turns pairwise judgments into weights and checks their consistency. CellCo's three technologies score within 0.013, so the choice depends on whose weights the board adopts.
:::
:::

[Session 3: Monte Carlo simulation of the new line's NPV, and the value of building in stages.]{.note-line}
